_README: Facts read off the sheets by eye, which the footprint fit then works within.
rotation: the placement angle at which the sheet's north symbol points up.
A footprint match cannot tell a building from itself turned around, and
on a symmetric plan it will happily choose either. So each anchor sheet's
north symbol -- a circle with a chord across it and a triangle standing on
that chord, apex pointing north -- was read unrotated, and the angle that
brings the apex upright is recorded here. Calibrated against SW5, whose
hand placement is rotation 0 and whose apex is drawn pointing up.
These are absolute, not adjustments: the fitted angle moves whenever
anything upstream changes, and a stored '+90' silently stops being right.
Draughtsmen square the symbol off, so the fit still refines by up to 20
degrees either side -- CARI's building really does sit on a diagonal.
ratio: the drawing scale, 1:N, where the sheet states it or prints its floor
area. Some GIS footprints cover much more ground than the drawing does --
SW9's outline is 6043 m2 against a drawn floor of 1702, NE3's is 441
against 97 -- and fitting to those stretches the plan to fill them. SE40
prints 'SCALE: 1:100'; the rest come from the INT/EXT areas in the title
block, a reading that reproduces hand-placed SW5-Floor1 as 1:150.0 exactly.
NW4 and SE8 have no legible north symbol -- NW4's sheet carries none and
SE8's only ring is the BCIT roundel -- so both keep the fitted angle and
want a look in the tracer.
_overruled_note: NE4, SE10, SE42 and CARI had a north reading too, but their footprint match is decisive and disagrees with it -- at the read bearing each drawing sits visibly off its outline (NE4 0.87 against 0.50, SE42 0.92 against 0.34). Their rings are detail markers, not north symbols, so those four are left to the fit. The rule that follows: geometry decides where it can, and the symbol only breaks a tie.
_CARI_note: Left to the fit, which puts it at 134. The only ring on CARI's sheet reads as a triangle on a diameter pointing north-west, but at 315 the drawing sits visibly off its footprint while at 134 the arms, notches and rotunda all land on it (IoU 0.83 against 0.65). That circle is a detail marker, not a north symbol.
